the activities of the enzymes of nucleotide biosynthesis are increased in cancer cells and that these increases correlate with the extent of malignancy of the neoplasm.
CTP synthase is increased in cancer cells and that this is a biochemical strategy of cancer.

the activities of the enzymes of purine synthesis, including CTP synthetases, increase in cancer cells, and that the increases correlate with the extent of malignancy and with the rate of growth of the tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the biochemical strategy of neoplastic transformation, with the metabolic alterations that are common to all cancer cells, irrespective of their tissue of origin, and those that are associated with the progressive increase in malignancy of the tumours.

the elucidation of the biochemical mechanisms of tumour progression, and the present report describes a biochemical alteration in the cancer cells that is linked to the increase of malignancy and is a manifestation of a progression-linked imbalance in the cancer cell.
the elucidation of biochemical alterations that are linked to tumour growth rate and to tumour progression and that may therefore be of prognostic value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CTP synthase activity is increased in all the tumour types examined, and that this is a transformation- and/or progression-linked alteration.
the activity of CTP synthetases is elevated in all the neoplasias studied so far, irrespective of the tissue of origin or species.
the increased activity of CTP synthetases in cancer cells reflects an increased demand of these cells for CTP.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activities of all the enzymes that are key to DNA and RNA synthesis are increased in cancer cells, while those that are key to the catabolism of nucleic acid components are decreased.
the increased CTP synthetases activity represents a biochemical strategy of cancer cell growth.
the activity of CTP synthetases is increased in all tumours examined, irrespective of their origin, extent of differentiation or growth rate, in both animals and man.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activity of CTP synthetases in cancer tissues is significantly higher than that in the corresponding normal tissues.
cancer cells increase their CTP synthetases activity.
